name: The Old Town Wall
desc: The city's first wall, 400 years old; long stretches pulled down for houses.

name: Crownhold
desc: The giant royal castle on its crag: two curtain walls, 26 towers and a 50 m keep.

name: The Crown Tower
desc: 50 m great keep, eight storeys: the throne room is on the fifth.

name: The Crowning Stone
desc: A prehistoric stone carried up from the river: every monarch is crowned on it.

name: The Grand Market
desc: Biggest market in the city: cloth, pots, poultry, cheese, everything; the Moot Hill rises in its corner.

name: Moot Hill
desc: A Bronze Age burial mound left in the Grand Market; the city's assemblies are still held on top.

name: The Kingstone
desc: A 6 m menhir at the crossroads where the North and West roads meet. Older than any road.

name: Wardenhouse - YOUR HOUSE
desc: Home of The Warden of the Stones, facing the Kingstone. Start here.

name: The Spice Bazaar
desc: A 160 m covered street of spice, silk and incense sellers.

name: Wool Hall
desc: Wool exchange: fleeces from a hundred hill farms are graded and sold.

name: Muster Square
desc: Parade ground below the castle where the city militia drills.

name: Shambles Market
desc: The butchers' street-market (bring a strong stomach).

name: The Sleeping Giant inn
desc: The oldest inn in the city, built against the Old Town wall.

name: The Three Kings' Table
desc: A portal tomb on the Minster lawn; the island was holy before the Minster was.

name: Stonehallow Minster
desc: Gothic cathedral on King's Isle; its spire reaches 120 m, the tallest thing in the realm.

name: The Grand Bridge
desc: Two stone spans across both arms of the river; the north span carries 14 shops.

name: The Royal Menagerie
desc: Lions, a bear, an elephant from the south and the King's white stags.

name: The Giant's Grave
desc: A 90 m long barrow kept as a lawn in the palace gardens.

name: Palace of the Seven Gardens
desc: The royal summer palace and its seven gardens: maze, parterres, orchard, water garden, lime walk, menagerie and the Giant's Grave.

name: The Queen's Maze
desc: A 66 m hedge maze with a sundial stone at its heart.

name: Flower Market
desc: Flowers, herbs and songbirds for the palace quarter.

name: Grain Exchange
desc: Corn factors shout prices under the great timber roof.

name: Merchant Palaces
desc: Four courtyard palaces of the great trading houses.

name: King's Quay
desc: Half a kilometre of stone quays, warehouses, treadwheel cranes and cogs from overseas.

name: Fish Market
desc: Fishwives, oysters and the catch of the morning boats.

name: The Ropewalk
desc: A shed 300 m long where hemp is twisted into ships' cables.

name: Harbour Light
desc: Lighthouse at the end of the breakwater guiding cogs into the river mouth.

name: The Star Citadel
desc: Five-pointed bastioned fortress guarding the river's entry into the city.

name: The Arsenal
desc: Where the city's crossbows, pikes and siege engines are built and stored.

name: Drill Field & Archery Butts
desc: Every man of the city must shoot at the butts on Sundays.

name: Camp of the Iron Host
desc: A standing camp of 2,000 soldiers: tents, horse lines and a palisade.

name: Siege Yard
desc: Trebuchets and mangonels being built and tested.

name: Cavalry Paddocks
desc: Grazing and training for the knights' horses.

name: Night Market
desc: Opens at dusk under lanterns: hot food, music, fortune-tellers.

name: The Lantern Playhouse
desc: Round wooden playhouse for 1,500: comedies, tragedies and riots.

name: Bear Garden
desc: Animal-baiting pit and its noisy galleries.

name: Bathhouse of the Swan
desc: Steam rooms, tubs and gossip.

name: Bathhouse of the Mermaid
desc: Steam rooms, tubs and gossip.

name: The Nine Sisters
desc: Nine little stones in a ring, kept inside the pleasure gardens; lovers meet here.

name: Lantern Gardens
desc: Pleasure gardens lit with a thousand lanterns on summer nights.

name: The Great Auditorium
desc: Stone amphitheatre seating 8,000 for proclamations, plays and tournaments.

name: Cattle Market
desc: Pens of cattle, sheep and pigs inside the South Gate.

name: Tanners' Reach
desc: Downwind and downstream: tanneries, dye vats in three colours, kilns, a bell foundry, glassworks and a brewery.

name: The Shipyard
desc: Four slipways building war cogs for the crown, with a sail loft and mast pond.

name: College of the Seven Stars
desc: A college of the university: hall, chapel, library and rooms round a grass court.

name: The Druids' Row
desc: Eight stones in a dead-straight line; the astronomers say it points at the midwinter sunrise.

name: Scholars' Hill University
desc: Three colleges, a library, an observatory, an anatomy theatre and the Hall of Disputations.

name: Book Market
desc: Copyists, maps, almanacs and forbidden books under the counter.

name: West Bridge
desc: Six arches and two corn mills where the scholars cross into the Westgate.

name: St. Bartholomew's Fair Field
desc: A fair field the size of the Old Town: tents, pavilions, stages, a jousting tiltyard, archery, a maypole. Busiest in late August.

name: Field of Rest
desc: The great cemetery beyond the walls.

name: Whitecross Abbey
desc: Benedictine abbey with its own farms, fishponds and bees.

name: Leper House of St. Lazarus
desc: Kept far outside the walls, with its own chapel and garden.

name: The Old Ring
desc: An Iron Age hillfort: three rings of ramparts on the hill; a hermit now lives inside.

name: Saltreed Marsh
desc: Reedbeds, herons and smugglers' paths.

name: Salt Pans
desc: Sea water evaporates in shallow pans; salt is the city's white gold.

name: South Down windmills
desc: Four post-mills grinding the southern harvest.

name: Haymarket
desc: Carters bring hay, straw and firewood down from the hills.

name: Brigid's Well & Stone
desc: A holy spring guarded by an ancient standing stone; pilgrims tie ribbons to it.

name: Pilgrims' Hospice
desc: Free beds and soup for pilgrims arriving from the north.

name: Mere Abbey
desc: Cistercian abbey on the shore of the Mirror Mere.

name: Royal Hunting Lodge
desc: The King's lodge deep in the Royal Forest.

name: Crownback Vineyards
desc: South-facing terraces of vines above the palace.

name: Horse Fair
desc: Horse dealers' field outside the West Gate.

name: Eastfold
desc: Fishing village on Gull Bay: huts on stilts, drying racks and boats on the shingle.

name: Raven Light
desc: Lighthouse on the cliffs of Raven Head.

name: The Sea Stones
desc: A tiny stone ring and a rock carved with cups and rings, on the windiest cliff in the realm.

name: Gull Rock Sea Fort
desc: Round fort on an island guarding the river mouth; reached only by boat.

name: Lantern Point
desc: Smugglers' village and lighthouse on the southern headland.
